Sub: Investments made by exempted trusts in recently downgraded companies
Advisory.

Sir,

The establishments exempted under Section 17(1)(a) and 17 (2) of the Employees”
Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 read with Para 27A of the
Employees Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 are required to follow the conditions as
delineated in Appendix ‘A’ to Para 27AA of the EPF Scheme, 1952.

2. The condition No.17 of the said Appendix stipulates that “7he Board of Trustees
shall invest the monies of the provident fund as per the directions of the Government from
time to time. Failure to make investments as per directions of the Government shall make
the Board of Trustees separately and liable to surcharge as may be imposed by the
Central Provident Fund Commissioner or his representative.”

3: Further attention is invited to condition No. 28 of the said Appendix ‘A’ that
stipulates “Jn the event of any loss to the trust as a result of any fraud, defalcation, wrong
investment decision etc., the employer shall be liable to make good the loss.”
Accordingly, the exempted establishments are supposed to recoup the loss incurred by the
trusts from its own source whenever there is any loss to the trust due to bad investments.

4. In this regard, it has come to notice that ratings of M/s. Amtek Auto, M/s. Jindal
Steel & Power Limited (JSPL) and some other companies have been downgraded in the
recent past. Accordingly, all the exempted establishments under your jurisdiction may be
advised to closely monitor companies in the Provident Fund portfolios of their respective
trusts that have been downgraded recently/likely to be downgraded in near future and
report deviation, if any, to this office at the earliest.

Yours faithfully,
